TITLE: LGTM caught 15 of 17 real advisories with 1 false alarm on the 17 fixes; the same model with only the diff caught 7
model.verdict: The local 27B model catches one advisory fewer than Sonnet 4.6, Haiku 4.5 and gpt-oss-120b (15 vs 16 of 17) but raises 1 false alarm against their 5–8, at no Bedrock cost
DEEPDIVE.sqli.headline: Django's raster band index went straight into PostGIS SQL: LGTM traced it, the plain LLM and Semgrep did not
DEEPDIVE.sqli.flaw: GHSA-mwm9-4648-f68q (CVE-2026-1207), django/django, CWE-89, advisory severity high. Adding spatial lookups to RasterField formatted the band index from the lookup tuple into the PostGIS SQL template unvalidated, so any user whose input an application passes as a raster lookup's band index could inject SQL.
DEEPDIVE.sqli.finding: CWE-89, Kev severity critical, django/contrib/gis/db/backends/postgis/operations.py:61 — check_raster() concatenates lookup.band_lhs/band_rhs into the SQL text with '%s, %s' % (...) instead of binding them, and band_rhs comes verbatim from the lookup tuple (lookups.py:87). Kev verdict: real (supported). A second finding flagged lookups.py:87 (CWE-89, critical, real).
DEEPDIVE.sqli.evidence: Cited operations.py:58–66 and lookups.py:82–87 (PR snapshot, i.e. the changed code, not base), opened with read_file after grep_repo 'band_lhs|band_rhs' and one investigate_base_code query on where band_lhs/band_rhs are set: 5 tool calls in that SQLi section. Policy passage: Django docs/topics/security.txt via search_policy.
DEEPDIVE.sqli.others: Plain LLM (same model): miss, answered safe. Semgrep: no findings on the vulnerable or the fix diff. LGTM on the fix commit: 0 findings (clean).
DEEPDIVE.authz.headline: Logged in is not authorised: LGTM caught khoj's subscription endpoint acting on any email the caller names
DEEPDIVE.authz.flaw: GHSA-hq4h-w933-jm6c (CVE-2024-52294), khoj-ai/khoj, CWE-639, advisory severity moderate. The billing PR added PATCH /api/subscription, which took the target customer's email from a query parameter instead of the logged-in user, so any authenticated user could cancel or resume anyone's Stripe subscription.
DEEPDIVE.authz.finding: CWE-639, Kev severity high, src/khoj/routers/subscription.py:85 — update_subscription is guarded only by @requires(["authenticated"]) and looks up and modifies the Stripe customer for a caller-supplied email, never comparing it with the requesting user. Kev verdict: real (supported). Two findings, both at line 85.
DEEPDIVE.authz.policy: No relevant policy passage: all 19 search_policy calls returned unrelated docs (notion/github integration guides, app README; relevance 0.06–0.33) and neither finding cites policy. The check compared against was code: the @requires(["authenticated"]) gate (subscription.py:82), configure.py authenticate() (63–79, outside the diff), grep for request.auth: no matches.
DEEPDIVE.authz.others: Plain LLM (same model): miss, answered safe. Semgrep: no findings on the vulnerable or the fix diff. LGTM on the fix commit: 0 findings (clean).
